text:
Lena (Sales): Sofia's team asked for an EU-only residency diagram, signed subprocessor list (last 12 mo), and a POC delivery checklist covering an on-prem/VPC option. Need to turn around ASAP.

Arun (Solutions Eng): Copy. Clarify: they want a high-level hosted flow to verify cross-border exposure AND a private deployment schematic with network controls?

Sofia (Customer CISO): Correct. Hosted flow to prove no egress to non-EU. Private/VPC sketch so our infra team can validate firewall/ACLs. Also include KMS handling and where logs live.

Fiona (Security): I'll assemble the subproc artifact. We provide a signed PDF + CSV export. I'll mark which subprocessors have EU-only deployments vs global. Note: telemetry vendor only ingests aggregated metrics for hosted customers unless they opt-in.

Arun (Solutions Eng): Quick ascii for hosted EU-only (will export SVG/PNG):

```
Client -> API Gateway (gateway.eu.redwood.ai)
            -> regional LB -> Inference cluster (eu-central-1)
                  -> GPU workers
                  -> KV cache (eu nodes only)
                  -> Object store (eu S3)
                  -> Audit logs -> Log store (eu-retention 90d)
```

Arun (Solutions Eng): For Private/VPC POC we show split-plane: control plane (managed) with minimal metadata vs data plane fully inside customer's VPC.

```
Redwood Control Plane (no customer data)
   
Customer VPC: app -> Private runtime (in VPC)
             -> Model weights in customer S3 (opt)
             -> Customer KMS (BYOK/HSM)
             -> Logs -> customer SIEM or push to secure bucket
```

Sofia (Customer CISO): Can you confirm KV cache replication policy — no replicas outside EU? And what happens if regional capacity is exhausted?

Fiona (Security): Confirmed: for customers who select EU-only residency we pin caches and compute to EU regions. If EU capacity exhausted the default behavior is fail-closed (requests return 503) for residency-protected customers. We can document an opt-in multiregion failover policy but that requires written consent.

Lena (Sales): Action items: Arun -> SVG + PNG diagrams, 1-page POC checklist (what we deliver + customer responsibilities). Fiona -> signed subproc CSV+PDF + retention table. Carlos -> short signable attestation referencing SOC2/GDPR and 30-day subprocessor notice. Delivery target: Thursday COB. Sofia okay?

Sofia (Customer CISO): Thursday COB is fine. Also please include a minimal ACL example and a sample DPA clause snippet we can show legal.

Arun (Solutions Eng): ACL snippet we recommend: 
``
- allow tcp/443 from CUSTOMER_APP_CIDR to PRIVATE_RUNTIME_CIDR
- allow tcp/22 from CUSTOMER_ADMIN_CIDR to management_proxy_ip (if customer consents)
- deny all else to PRIVATE_RUNTIME_CIDR
```

Carlos (Legal): I'll draft the attestation: list of current subprocessors, 30-day notification for changes, statement on data locations, and reference to our standard DPA. We avoid committing to special clauses until contract stage.

Fiona (Security): Note re: telemetry: for Private deployments we can disable outbound telemetry entirely on request. For Dedicated we support customer-managed telemetry endpoints.

procurement-bot: Reminder: attach NDA for full subprocessor list disclosure.

Lena (Sales): I'll coordinate the email to Sofia after we assemble files. Tagging owners: @Arun (diagrams + checklist), @Fiona (subproc + retention), @Carlos (attestation).

Arun (Solutions Eng): ETA 5 hours for uploads to this thread.

Fiona (Security): I'll push signed CSV by EOD and will DM procurement contact for NDA.

Lena (Sales): Great, thanks everyone :thumbsup:

Sofia (Customer CISO): Thanks team, will review when received.
